deities: Dwarkadhish (Lord Krishna as Dwarkanath/King of Dwarka - black marble idol, without flute or peacock feather)
festivals: Hindola festival (13 days, Shravana - July-August, the temple's main festival)

history.dynasty: Scindia (Gwalior State) patronage; built by Seth Gokul Das Parikh, treasurer of the Gwalior State, with approval and donation from Maharaja Daulatrao Scindia
history.summary: One of the oldest and largest temples of Mathura city, where Krishna is worshipped in his royal Dwarkanath/Dwarkadhish form (King of Dwarka) alongside Radharani - a striking black marble idol of Dwarkanath with a white marble idol of Radha. The current structure was built in 1814 by Seth Gokul Das Parikh, treasurer of the then Gwalior State (Scindia), with approval and donation from Shrimant Daulatrao Scindia, Maharajah of Gwalior; Gokuldas was a devotee of the third Gaddi of the Pushtimarg, whose seat is the Dwarkadhish temple at Kankroli, Rajasthan. Architecture is Rajasthani in character (one source describes a Rajasthani-Mughal blend) with the grand Swarg Dwar (Heavenly Gate) entrance, carved facades, a tall shikhara and a large courtyard with smaller shrines. The main festival is the 13-day Hindola festival in Shravana, when the icons are placed in a decorated jhoola (swing) adorned with gold and silver ornaments for special darshan. Distinct from the famous Dwarkadhish Temple (Jagat Mandir) at Dwarka, Gujarat - this is the Mathura shrine.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Kheria Airport, Agra, about 46 km from Mathura; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction (MTJ) - the temple stands in central Mathura near Holi Gate/Naya Bazar, a short drive from the station.
travel.road: Located at Holi Gate, Naya Bazar in the old city of Mathura; reachable by auto-rickshaw and taxi within the city; well connected by road to Delhi and Agra.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami and the Hindola festival (Shravana) are the peak celebration times but very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning session reported as 6:30 AM-11:00 AM (per wanderlog); evening session timings are not published in the consulted sources - verify locally before travel.
